topics.name: Fundamental Theorem of Arithmetic (HCF and LCM)

questions.title: LCM of 28, 44 and 132
questions.text: The LCM of three numbers 28, 44 and 132 is:
steps: ④ LCM = every prime, HIGHEST power
questions.remember:
LCM: every prime, highest power.
HCF: only common primes, lowest power.
questions.trap: Multiplying all three numbers gives a common multiple, not the LEAST one.

questions.title: Co-prime numbers with product 553: HCF
questions.text: If the product of two co-prime numbers is 553, then their HCF is:
steps: ① Co-prime ⟹ no common factor except 1
② HCF = the highest COMMON factor
③ Their only common factor is 1
questions.remember: Co-prime ⟹ HCF = 1, and then LCM = their product.
questions.tryit: Two co-prime numbers have product 117. Find their LCM.

questions.title: Greatest number dividing 134 and 188 with remainders
questions.text: The greatest number which divides both 134 and 188, leaving remainders 4 and 6 respectively, is:
questions.remember:
'Greatest number that divides' ⟹ HCF.
'Smallest number divisible by' ⟹ LCM.
questions.trap: Forgetting to subtract the remainders. 13 is common too, but not the greatest.
questions.tryit: Greatest number dividing 281 and 1249, leaving remainders 5 and 7.

questions.title: Assertion–Reason: HCF 17, product 5780
questions.text:
Assertion (A): If the product of two numbers is 5780 and their HCF is 17, then their LCM is 340.
Reason (R): HCF is always a factor of LCM.
opts: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.
steps: ① A: HCF × LCM = product of the two numbers
③ R: HCF divides both numbers; LCM is a multiple of both
④ ⟹ HCF divides LCM  ✓ R true
⑤ But A used the PRODUCT rule, not R
questions.remember: HCF × LCM = product of the two numbers
questions.trap: Two true statements ≠ option (a). Always ask: does R explain A?
questions.tryit: Can two numbers have HCF 24 and LCM 540?

questions.title: Longest ruler for a hall 9.75 × 6.75 × 5.25 m
questions.text: A hall has a length of 9.75 m, breadth of 6.75 m and height of 5.25 m. What is the length of the longest unmarked ruler that can exactly measure the dimensions of the hall?
steps: ② Remove decimals: 975 cm, 675 cm, 525 cm
questions.remember: Convert decimals into whole numbers first.
questions.trap: Writing '75' without the unit. Write 75 cm (or 0.75 m).
questions.tryit: 48 French, 80 Hindi, 144 English teachers: same subject, same number per room. Minimum rooms?

questions.title: Three bells every 5, 6, 8 minutes: 10 a.m. to 7 p.m.
questions.text: Three bells in a park toll at intervals of 5, 6 and 8 minutes respectively. They all toll together when the park opens at 10:00 a.m. How many more times do they all toll together till the park is closed at 7:00 p.m.?
steps: ⑤ Every 2 h: 12 noon, 2 p.m., 4 p.m., 6 p.m.
questions.tryit: Traffic lights change every 48, 72 and 108 s. Together at 7 a.m. — when next?

questions.title: Prove that √5 is irrational
questions.text: Prove that √5 is an irrational number.
steps: ① Assume √5 is rational: √5 = p/q, p, q co-prime, q ≠ 0
③ 5 divides p² ⟹ 5 divides p (5 is prime)
⑤ So 5 divides q², hence 5 divides q
⑥ 5 divides both p and q: contradiction!
questions.trap: Skipping '5 is prime, so 5 divides p'. Examiners look for that reason.

questions.title: Given √3 irrational, prove 2 + 3√3 is irrational
questions.text: Given that √3 is an irrational number, prove that (2 + 3√3) is an irrational number.
steps: ② Assume 2 + 3√3 = r, where r is rational
questions.remember: If they give you an irrational number, USE it. Don't re-prove it.
questions.trap: 'Rational + irrational is irrational' is a fact, not a proof. Show the steps.
questions.tryit: Given √2 is irrational, prove 5 + 3√2 is irrational.
